title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve, ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. The canonical P^1-bundle attached to X/S is P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)), the projectivized bundle of first-order jets of ω. The surrounding pages study projective connections on X/S, meaning connections on this P^1-bundle. Relative to a reference connection c_0 they are given by quadratic differentials φ(dt)^2. On the previous page Grothendieck reduces horizontality of a section to the Riccati equation dλ/dt + λ^2 = φ.

This page (§1.6) describes a section of P intrinsically.
- A section is a line-bundle quotient σ: P^1(ω) → L.
- A linear map P^1(ω) → L is the same as a first-order differential operator D: ω → L.
- The restriction of σ to the subbundle ω⊗Ω^1 = ω^2 ⊂ P^1(ω) is the symbol γ_0: ω^2 → L, i.e. γ_0 ∈ Γ(L⊗ω^{-2}). It is characterized by D(fω) − fD(ω) = γ_0(ω·df).
- P has a canonical section, the quotient P^1(ω) → ω whose kernel is ω^2.
- The section given by D meets the canonical section exactly where ker σ_x = ω^2_x, i.e. where γ_0 vanishes. These are the points where D degenerates to order 0, the 'singular points' of D.
- L is generated by the D(ω) because σ is surjective.
- Where γ_0 is invertible it gives a canonical isomorphism L ≅ ω^2.

Conclusion: on the open set U where D is nonsingular there is a unique projective connection making the section horizontal. In local terms this is λ ↦ φ = λ' + λ^2.

The next page treats extension across the degeneracy points. The condition is local: λ may have at most a simple pole there, with principal part fixed so that λ' + λ^2 stays pole-free (residue 1). Geometrically, along the canonical section σ there is a field of second-order section-elements transverse to σ. A section σ' is horizontal for some (then unique) projective connection on X iff σ' osculates this field to order 2 wherever it meets σ.

In modern terms: write λ = y'/y. Then λ' + λ^2 = φ becomes the Hill/Sturm–Liouville equation y'' = φy. Horizontal sections correspond to solutions y, i.e. to developing data of the sl_2-oper/projective structure. The points where a horizontal section meets the oper (canonical) section are the zeros of y. The problem served is the dictionary between projective connections, sections of the canonical P^1-bundle and Riccati equations, presumably as preparation for Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs and Cartier-operator questions in characteristic p.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The symbol formula D(fω) − fD(ω) = γ_0(ω·df) and the identification γ_0 ∈ Γ(L⊗ω^{-2}) are correct.

On the previous page the uniqueness claim for the first-order Riccati equation should only need the value at a point, not 'value and derivative'. Grothendieck himself flags a possible 'facteur 2' in the formula λ' + λ^2; normalization constants are uncertain.
Several sentences in the middle of the page are illegible, so the exact argument for the canonical trivialization of L at nonsingular points cannot be fully verified.

ideas.what: Sections of P(P^1(ω)) correspond to quotients P^1(ω) → L, equivalently to first-order differential operators D: ω → L, with symbol γ_0 ∈ Γ(L⊗ω^{-2})
ideas.modern_name: jet-bundle description of sections; principal symbol of a differential operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (EGA IV §16 formalism of principal parts)
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16 (principal parts, differential operators); the specific application to curves is unsure

ideas.what: A section of P meets the canonical (oper) section exactly at the zeros of the symbol γ_0 (degeneracy points of D)
ideas.modern_name: intersection of a section with the Hodge/oper flag; zeros of solutions / branch points
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gunning on projective structures; Beilinson–Drinfeld opers)

ideas.what: On the nondegeneracy locus there is a unique projective connection making a given section horizontal; it extends across degeneracy points iff the section osculates a canonical second-order transverse field there (λ has a simple pole with residue 1 and λ' + λ^2 is regular)
ideas.modern_name: Riccati/Schwarzian correspondence between projective structures and sections of the oper P^1-bundle; regularity of the oper at zeros of y
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riccati, Schwarz); modern form by Gunning and Beilinson–Drinfeld

missed.claim: An intrinsic, base-general (X/S) characterization of which sections of the canonical P^1-bundle P(P^1(Ω^1)) are horizontal for some projective connection: second-order contact with a canonical transverse field along the oper section. This is equivalent to well-known facts about opers and zeros of solutions of y'' = φy, so it is likely not new to specialists.
missed.quote: il y a une trivialisation de L, canonique ... sur l'ouvert des pts où elle est non singulière, une connexion ... unique qui la rend horizontale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck working out an oper-style formalism of projective connections over a general base around 1972. It is plausibly aimed at characteristic p (Cartier operator), where such formulations relate to dormant opers (Mochizuki), but this page does not reach p.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean intrinsic reformulation of classical projective-connection/Riccati facts in jet-bundle language. Mathematically standard, though of historical interest as an early oper-like formalism.
